newsitem.title: USA: US growth to pick up in 2nd half - KeyCorp economist.
newsitem.headline: US growth to pick up in 2nd half - KeyCorp economist.

text.p: U.S. economic growth, after pausing in the second quarter following blistering growth in the first quarter, will pick up in the second half of the year and eventually lead to another credit tightening by the Federal Reserve, KeyCorp chief economist Kenneth Mayland said.

Gross domestic product expanded at a 5.9 percent annualized rate in the first quarter, but should slow to about 1.75 percent growth in the second quarter before expanding again to a 3.0 to 3.5 percent in the second half, Mayland said in an interview.
With the stronger growth, inflation should also pick up as the year progresses, he said.

"Some portion of the good inflation performance of the second quarter was related to a slowdown in consumer spending," Mayland said. "Consumers were taking a breather," and manufacturers were unable to pass on price increases.

However, strong job and income growth, a "wealth effect" stemming from recent strong gains in the stock market, a surge in mortgage refinancings that creates disposable income, a possible tax cut and high consumer confidence levels all point to stronger consumer spending, he said.
That, in turn, "will be a better environment for manufacturers and retailers to sneak through modest price increases," Mayland said.

After Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony Tuesday, Mayland said the Fed "certainly won't raise rates at the August 19 meeting." Instead, a more likely time to see the Fed move toward higher rates will be the mid-November Federal Open Market Committee meeting.
